end.summary:
Practised that a freely suspended magnet settles roughly north–south, with its north pole pointing north.
Discussed making a simple compass: keep the magnet/needle free to move so it settles and shows the north–south line.
Mahi gave two unaided correct responses about the north-pointing end and the north–south line.
Mahi did not yet explain that Earth behaves like a giant magnet.
The misconception that a compass points north because the North is cold remained uncorrected at the end.
end.parentNote: Asha practised using a freely moving magnet to find the north–south direction and reviewed the labelled north pole. Mahi correctly described the needle settling and showing the north–south line. They mixed up the reason a compass points north, saying it is because the North is cold; this was not corrected by the end. At home, ask Mahi to make or observe a simple compass and explain that Earth behaves like a giant magnet.
